subject: NYFT (DTA 810139)
observation: NYFT supplied motor fuel to Tunyung; John Quock is named as Tunyung principal and MT-338 signatory. Tunyung held municipal supply contracts; M & Q Trucking was an NYFT affiliate.
limits: Blatt recalled deliveries but could not guarantee all; no independent complete shipment ledger or registry/license match to other Tunyung/Tun Yung or Conlo entities. Principal/signatory is not a shareholder percentage.

subject: NYFT books
observation: Taxes initially billed; NYFT credited qualifying exempt resales by reducing Tunyung receivable and sales accounts on its books.
limits: Book credit, not cash reimbursement or another receipt. Do not treat all claimed exempt sales as substantiated.

subject: Tunyung (payment attributed by decision)
observation: The decision reports one payment, allocated by Abbey Blatt to the earliest March 1988 invoice.
limits: No exact date, method, bank, account or instrument independently acquired; not a verified personal payment by Quock. ALJ and Tribunal are procedural versions, not independent receipts; distinct from 1983 Lesez/SMI transaction.

subject: NYFT judgment creditor
observation: P53/P54 report Kings County: principal USD 5343818.67 plus interest/costs, total USD 7277169.72. P55 reports New York County and total USD 7277189.72. Sources state NYFT could not collect on the judgment.
limits: USD 20 and county conflict unresolved; amount field intentionally blank. Same reported debt/judgment, not two awards. No original judgment/index number obtained; noncollection is as reported in these records, not a present-day collection-status check. Never sum principal, interest/costs, debt and receipt.

subject: DTA 810139;810140;810253
observation: Tribunal corrects ALJ Conclusion H: exemption only to extent substantiated; DTA 810139 otherwise denied, other two petitions denied, notices sustained as modified.
limits: 1997 blanket cancellation is not the controlling 1998 disposition. Neither blanket exoneration nor a finding all Tunyung sales were fictitious; no claim about exhaustion of judicial review.
